_description: The gate discipline as data. scripts/trace-report.mjs reads this instead of hardcoding stage names; the analyser names no stage. Editing THIS file is how the discipline changes. `checks.<name>.chain` is the ONE readable view of the stages a gate script runs, in order: package.json defines what runs, scripts/docs-check.mjs derives the chain from it and fails on any difference, and no other file lists the stages. Docs: .cursor/brain/VERIFICATION.md.
_phaseMeaning: The web siblings gate a scaffold phase that skips the stages needing a build until the first deploy. MEASURED here 2026-08-30: the whole gate is 8.7s (per-stage timings: .cursor/brain/VERIFICATION.md) — this gate has no stage that needs a build, so a phase switch would be machinery gating nothing. Recorded as a decision, not an omission; revisit if a native build or a Maestro run ever enters the gate.

verify:iter.description: iterate: the seconds-long check run per change
verify:iter.chain: check-hooks -> lint:oxlint -> typecheck -> lint-changed -> iterate-tests -> mutation-scope.test

verify.description: the offline gate: every check CI runs except the network-bound ones
verify.chain: check-hooks -> check-version-holds -> check-engines-floor -> check-test-siblings --range -> docs-check -> lint:oxlint -> format:check -> typecheck -> lint -> test:scripts -> test:coverage

verify:ci.description: the CI chain, and what pre-push runs

verify:native.description: machine parity with the Expo tooling, offline

test:one.description: one jest test file, through the tracer

docs:check.description: mechanical doc drift: paths, scripts, sentinels, versions, command table, dead docs, agent-memory imports, the chain view against package.json, hand-written retellings and compositions of it; the push budget vs traced pushes of the same phase (report only)

ci._description: Data for scripts/docs-check.mjs § ciSteps/rulesetContexts. allowedRunSteps lists every `run:` step in a PR-triggered workflow that legitimately runs outside `verify` (install/tooling steps, and the advisory expo-doctor step), each with the reason it is not a check that belongs in the gate. rulesetContextAllowlist is for a required status check produced by something other than this repo's own workflows (a third-party GitHub App) — empty today.

allowedRunSteps.reason: pins the npm version the lock file needs; not a check
Expo doctor, advisory only (continue-on-error), never blocks a PR
Hermes bundle budget: a full expo export of both platforms, the heaviest stage the repo has, so a CI-only lane (job bundle-budget) like the weekly mutation run; the same script runs locally
lists a change to the gate or an added suppression on a pull request until a reviewer labels it; the labels exist only on the pull request event, so no local chain can judge them

docs._description: Data for scripts/docs-check.mjs. sentinels = verbatim fragments of the tier law that may live only in AGENTS.md; versions = doc names -> package names compared with package-lock.json (node -> .nvmrc); stageWords = a stage of the verify chains -> the words the docs use for it besides its script name (a line outside the chain view that names enough distinct stages, or two parts of one script, is a retelling).
sentinels: never shortened by what the diff touched
Legal at any time, in any lane, never a violation
Parallel lanes never run heavy stages
A skipped stage is printed, never silent

suites._description: Ceilings on the device suite. It is counted in INVARIANTS, not screens (AGENTS.md § the gate): a route earns a Maestro flow only when it brings an invariant the existing specs do not measure. A suite over its ceiling is a finding, and so is a ceiling more than twice the measurement — that high it flags nothing. Raise a number on a measurement plus a DECISIONS.md line, like a size budget.

commit.description: Husky pre-commit: staged autofix, TDD sibling gate, repo-wide checks. Those run as direct commands, not traced npm scripts, so this moment is declared for completeness.

push.description: Husky pre-push -> verify:ci. Runs unconditionally, never shortened by what the diff touched.
push._budget: NO SECONDS HERE, deliberately, and this matters more in a template than anywhere else. A committed number of seconds describes ONE machine and nothing in the file says which, so every fork inherits a ceiling it may be unable to meet and reads red from its third push - measured ratio between the workstation that set the old numbers and a two-core runner: 5.6x and 10.5x on the same two suites. The gate calibrates a baseline from its OWN first `budgetBaselineMinRuns` runs, per phase, keeps it in the gitignored .gate-budget.json beside the tracer log, and reports drift past `budgetDriftRatio`. The baseline ratchets DOWN by itself when the gate gets faster, the same shape a lint or type baseline uses; it rises only when someone deletes the file, which is the honest way to say this is the new normal. `budgetWindow` keeps one bad day from poisoning p90. A fresh clone starts with no baseline, no red reading, and calibrates to its own hardware.
